meta.description: Semantic layer — exact definitions of every KPI. The dashboard, SQL layer, reports and any LLM narration must cite these definitions.
meta.disclosure: Synthetic, seeded dataset — fully reproducible. Methods are the story.
meta.source_data: data/raw/orders.csv (12,000 orders) + data/processed/master_orders.csv (21,066 item rows, 9,933 orders)
meta.convention_note: Revenue = SUM(line_total) over orders with status Delivered or Processing (Cancelled and Returned excluded). Pinned by tests/test_dashboard_consistency.py and scripts/decision_layer.py via the valid_orders definition (sql/02_data_cleaning.sql, python/eda/01_eda_preprocessing.py).

revenue.definition: Revenue across the 3-year window from orders that are Delivered or Processing. Cancelled and Returned orders are excluded (the same rule as valid_orders).

gross_margin.definition: Gross profit as a share of revenue.

completed_orders.definition: Orders with status Delivered (of 12,000 placed; 9,312 delivered).

active_customers.definition: Distinct customers with at least one Delivered or Processing order (revenue-eligible). Of 2,000 customer records: 1,999 ordered, 8 only Cancelled/Returned, 1 never ordered — hence 1,991.

churn_model.definition: Leakage-free churn model: features strictly before the 2024-07-03 cutoff, label = no purchase (Delivered or Returned) in the following 180 days. Model chosen by 5-fold CV on the training split; the selected model is scored once on a held-out 20%. Published per-customer scores are out-of-fold for training customers and holdout predictions for test customers — in-sample refit probabilities are never published.
churn_model.caveat: Honest post-leakage numbers; real churn models rarely score 0.9+ without leakage. The 23.54% prevalence is a MODEL LABEL RATE on the scored population, not a business churn rate. Rolling-origin backtest AUC 0.56-0.67 across five cutoffs — see reports/churn_temporal_backtest.json. Full evidence in reports/churn_model_metrics.json.

cooling_off_customers.definition: Medium churn-risk band — the win-back audience.
cooling_off_customers.caveat: Historical spend, NOT future revenue at risk.

rfm_segments.definition: RFM quintiles + K-Means into 8 named segments.

bcg_matrix.definition: BCG-style PROXY, not the classic matrix: products are split on median units sold (x) and median gross margin (y) into Star / Cash Cow / Question Mark / Dog. No market-share or market-growth data exists in the dataset.

revenue_forecast.definition: HISTORICAL backtest, not a live projection: ensemble of linear trend + Holt-Winters fitted through Dec 2024 and projected for Jan–Jun 2025, bootstrap 95% CI.
revenue_forecast.caveat: The horizon is in the past relative to publication — this is a holdout evaluation of the method. Rolling-origin MASE 0.68 loses to the drift baseline (0.468) and the 95% band covered only 9.5% of actuals; see reports/forecast_backtest.md.

purchase.definition: An order with status Delivered or Returned. Cancelled orders never transacted; Processing is not yet a purchase.

cohort_retention.definition: Customers grouped by first-purchase month; retention M_k = share with >=1 purchase k months after the cohort month. M0 = 100% by definition.
cohort_retention.verified_pattern: Month-1 retention appears to rise for late-2024 cohorts — this is a RIGHT-CENSORING ARTIFACT, not a real improvement: those cohorts have a compressed observation window (12 of 36 cohorts have <12 months observed; Nov 2024 has 1 month, Dec 2024 has 0). Do not read it as improving retention.

order_funnel.definition: Placed (all 12,000) -> Delivered (9,312). Statuses are mutually exclusive, so 'Returned' is its own exit (1,223), not subtracted from 'Delivered'.

mom_delta.definition: Month-over-month change of a KPI (latest vs previous month). Alert threshold: 10% relative change.

clv_concentration.definition: Share of projected customer lifetime value held by the top decile.

winback_experiment.definition: DESIGN ONLY — no experiment has been run. See docs/experiment_design_winback.md.
winback_experiment.note: Expanded pool = core Medium band union RFM About To Sleep + At Risk (575, of which 244 already in core), so 772 — not 1,023 (which double-counted the overlap). Its own measured 90-day baseline is 50.7%.

churn_calibration.definition: Probability quality and decision thresholds for the churn model (fit/cal/test 64/16/20) on scripts/churn_data.py's frame.
churn_calibration.threshold_selection: expected-profit maximizing on the calibration slice; cost model: C=INR250/contact, r=15% recovery, V=INR13,292.2 (mean observed 180-day spend of retained customers)
churn_calibration.caveat: Profit figures are expected values under illustrative assumptions; no campaign has been run. Calibration is NOT uniformly helpful here: the pipeline's isotonic fit on 1,277 out-of-fold training predictions improves holdout Brier 0.1726 to 0.1715, while the separate script's isotonic fit on only 256 calibration rows overfits (Brier 0.172 to 0.1815, slope 0.7875 to 0.13). Both results are reported, not averaged away.
churn_calibration.correction_note: Values re-derived 2026-11-18 after unifying the purchase definition (Delivered or Returned) across cohort retention, churn labels and experiment baselines, and replacing in-sample scoring with out-of-fold + holdout scoring. Earlier registry values (roc_auc 0.6484, pr_auc 0.3616, prevalence 0.2535, n 1586, brier_raw 0.1957, t*=0.10) came from the older definition/split and are superseded. An earlier 2026-10-17 correction removed a set of figures (0.6489 / 0.3664 / 0.1952 / 0.1811 / 0.0299) that were not reproducible from the committed code and data.
churn_calibration.temporal_backtest: reports/churn_temporal_backtest.json — 5 rolling origins, CV AUC 0.5611, 0.5515, 0.5861, 0.6378, 0.6710; the 80/20 split is NOT described as a temporal split.

forecast_backtest.definition: Rolling-origin backtest of the revenue forecast vs naive baselines (10 origins x 3 horizons).
forecast_backtest.mase_scale: in-sample seasonal-naive MAE (|y_t - y_t-12| mean) = INR 1,023,756
forecast_backtest.verdict: Ensemble loses to the drift baseline; shipped bootstrap CI covers only 9.5% of actuals. See reports/forecast_backtest.md.
forecast_backtest.caveat: Synthetic revenue series; methods transfer, numbers do not.

discount_analysis.definition: Cost and break-even economics of the discount ladder (python/pricing/elasticity.py).
discount_analysis.grain: order line items, valid orders only (Delivered + Processing)

kpis.margin_pct_of_list: profit / (line_total / (1 - discount_pct)) — margin as a share of LIST price, so depths are comparable
kpis.break_even_volume_lift: (margin_pct_of_list at 0%) / (margin_pct_of_list at depth) - 1 — volume uplift needed just to hold total margin flat
kpis.volume_response_detected: Kruskal-Wallis test of quantity across discount depths, alpha = 0.05

measured_results.significant_category: Sports (p=0.003) with a NEGATIVE effect of -6.96% at 20pp

discount_analysis.caveat: Observational data: in this synthetic dataset discount depth is assigned randomly, so the measured association is not automatically causal. The scenario engine reports what would have to be true (break-even lift) rather than claiming what will happen.

winback_campaign.definition: Expected-value economics of the win-back campaign on the cooling-off churn band (python/pricing/winback.py).

cost_model.note: Same C/r/V as the churn model in reports/churn_calibration_metrics.json — a single source of truth.

kpis.expected_net_revenue_per_contact: P(churn) x recovery_rate x retained_value - contact_cost. Revenue before COGS: retained_value is 180-day SPEND, so at the 54.0% gross margin ≈₹167 of contribution per contact.
kpis.break_even_churn_probability: contact_cost / (recovery_rate x retained_value) — equals the churn model Bayes threshold by construction. On a margin basis the break-even rises to ≈23.2%.

measured_results.basis: Revenue before COGS. The 'profit' key names are retained for compatibility with reports/winback_economics.json; read them as expected NET REVENUE. Margin-adjusted: ≈₹167 contribution per contact, break-even ≈23.2%.

winback_campaign.caveat: Every figure is an expectation under stated assumptions — no campaign has been run. The recovery rate is not measured and is the most sensitive input, which is why a sensitivity grid is published rather than a point estimate alone.

forecast_challenger.definition: Rolling-origin challenger evaluation against the drift baseline (scripts/forecast_challenger.py).
forecast_challenger.protocol: Identical to scripts/forecast_backtest.py — imported constants and baseline functions.

measured_results.finding: Seasonality hurts on this dataset: seasonal_naive 2.05 and holt_winters 0.56 both lose to the seasonality-free trend model.
